syncStatus.label: Sync status
syncStatus.announceConflict_one: A new sync conflict needs your decision.
syncStatus.announceSchemaTooOld: The sync dataset was created by a newer Aperio version. Please update the app.
syncStatus.notifyConflictBody_one: A sync conflict needs your decision. Open Aperio to resolve it.
syncStatus.notifyConflictBody_other: {{count}} sync conflicts need your decision. Open Aperio to resolve them.

syncSchemaTooOld.title: Update required
syncSchemaTooOld.body: The existing sync dataset was created with a newer version of Aperio and is not compatible with this version.
syncSchemaTooOld.hint: Update the app to resume syncing. Your local data stays readable in the meantime, but no further changes are written to the sync store.

syncStaleResume.title: This device was offline for a while
syncStaleResume.body: Some changes were compacted on the sync store. The current data state will now be downloaded in full (snapshot from {{time}}).
syncStaleResume.mergeHint: Local changes you made while offline are kept in the local push queue and will be sent to the other devices on the next sync round.

syncAccountsConnect.title: Reconnect accounts
syncAccountsConnect.body: We pulled in your accounts from the sync store, but the passwords and tokens are stored only on each device. Please re-attach the credentials for the following accounts so this device can reach them too.
syncAccountsConnect.hint: You can also dismiss this dialog and reconnect later from Settings → Accounts. Until then, calendars and tasks from these accounts will be unavailable on this device.
syncAccountsConnect.oauthHint: Opens the sign-in page in your default browser.
syncAccountsConnect.errorAuth: The credentials were rejected. Please check and try again.
syncAccountsConnect.errorNetwork: Network error while reaching the account.
syncAccountsConnect.errorInvalidInput: The input is not valid for this account type.
syncAccountsConnect.errorEmpty: Please enter a value before saving.

calendars.hint: Default reminders that apply to events without their own reminder. Useful for iCloud calendars: iOS “Default Alert Times” aren't written into the event itself, so without a default here the alarm doesn't show in Aperio.
calendars.empty: No calendars yet — add an account first.

contacts.privacyBody: Aperio syncs your contacts directly with the connected providers and keeps names, email addresses, phone numbers, birthdays, and organisation fields in memory so search and the attendees picker stay responsive.
contacts.privacyProvidersIntro: What each provider collects and how long they retain it is governed by their own privacy policies:
contacts.providerPolicyOthers: For CardDAV, iCloud, and Exchange accounts the privacy policy of your server applies.
contacts.syncBody: All writable address books sync at app start and at the configured interval. Heavy read-only directories (GAL / Suggested People / Other Contacts / Workspace Directory) only pull on demand.
contacts.includeDirectoriesHint: When ticked, every sync — manual and periodic — also pulls the read-only directories (GAL / Suggested People / Other Contacts / Workspace Directory). May take several minutes depending on account size. The setting is remembered across restarts.
contacts.includeDirectoriesEnabled: Read-only directories will be included on the next sync.
contacts.includeDirectoriesDisabled: Read-only directories will be skipped on the next sync.
contacts.cacheBody: Drops the in-memory snapshots of every external address book. Your own local contacts and the local “Contacts” folder are not affected — the next sync re-pulls provider data.
contacts.cacheCleared_zero: Cache cleared — no connected accounts to notify.
contacts.cacheClearFailed: Couldn't fully clear the cache. See log for details.

sync.compactDone: Snapshot taken, {{deleted}} old log files deleted.
sync.adapterBody: Pick a storage location for your sync dataset. Currently supported: local directory (e.g. a mounted NAS). WebDAV, SFTP and cloud services follow later.
sync.adapterPathHint: Absolute path to the shared directory. macOS example: /Volumes/NAS/aperio. Windows example: \\server\aperio.
sync.adapterWebdavUrlHint: Full WebDAV collection URL. For Nextcloud typically https://<host>/remote.php/dav/files/<user>/<folder>/. Path must end with a slash.
sync.adapterWebdavPasswordHint: Stored encrypted in your system keychain and never synced. Leave blank when editing only the URL or username — the stored password is reused.
sync.adapterSftpPathHint: Absolute path on the server, e.g. /home/alice/aperio. The configured SSH user must have write access.
sync.adapterSftpPasswordHint: Stored encrypted in your system keychain. Leave blank when editing only the host/user — the stored password is reused.
sync.adapterSftpKeyPathHint: Absolute path to your SSH private key (PEM or OpenSSH format). Typically under ~/.ssh/ on Linux/macOS, e.g. /home/alice/.ssh/id_ed25519. The key itself never leaves this device.
sync.adapterSftpKeyPassphraseHint: Optional, only for encrypted keys. Stored in your system keychain. Leave blank when editing only the path.
sync.adapterSftpHostKeyMismatch: Warning: the server's host key changed since the last connection. This could be a harmless server reinstall — or an attack. Verify the new fingerprint with the server admin before reconnecting.
sync.sftpTrustNewBody: This is the first time Aperio is connecting to this SFTP server. Verify that the fingerprint below matches what the server administrator gave you out-of-band (e.g. via a phone call or a separate channel) before accepting.
sync.sftpTrustChangedBody: The server's host key is different from the one Aperio pinned previously. This can mean a harmless server reinstall — or a man-in-the-middle attack. Verify the new fingerprint with the server administrator before accepting; cancel and abort otherwise.
sync.sftpTrustVerifyHint: Compare the SHA256 fingerprint against the one the administrator provided. The strings must match exactly, character for character.
sync.sftpPinHint: Aperio will reject any connection to this server whose key doesn't match. Drop the pin when you know the server's key has rotated (e.g. after a reinstall).
sync.sftpForgetPinConfirm: Drop the pinned fingerprint for {{hostPort}}? The next connection will go through the first-use confirmation dialog again.
sync.sustainedFailureBanner: The last few sync rounds failed in a row. Aperio is now retrying less often (exponential backoff, capped at 30 minutes). "Sync now" runs a fresh attempt immediately; otherwise the next periodic round will resume the normal cadence once a round succeeds.
sync.protocolBody: Recent sync rounds, newest first. Useful for diagnosing transient failures or verifying that periodic rounds are firing as expected. Kept for the last ~200 rounds.
sync.protocolClearConfirm: Drop every entry in the sync protocol? This only affects the local diagnostic history; no sync data is touched.
sync.previewBody: If a sync dataset already exists at the chosen path, the onboarding shows you the known devices. You then decide whether to adopt it or start fresh.
sync.deviceNameHint: How should other devices show this device? Example: "Desktop PC", "MacBook".
sync.previewEmpty: No sync dataset found at the path. "Start fresh" will create one now.
sync.previewAcceptBody: Downloads the existing snapshot and all newer log files and merges them into this device. Local changes you made before onboarding are NOT lost — they upload on the next sync.
sync.previewAdoptBody: Overwrites the sync storage's meta.json with a fresh dataset registering only this device. Other devices won't see their own entries any more — their next sync will report them as a "new device".
sync.previewAdoptConfirm: Really start fresh? Other devices lose their sync link to this dataset.
sync.onboardingFresh: Connected — this device is the first on the dataset.
sync.errorNotFound: No dataset found at the path.
sync.errorSchemaTooOld: Sync dataset needs a newer Aperio version.
sync.errorEncryption: Encrypted dataset, but no password configured.
sync.e2eEnableHint: All log files and snapshots are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they leave this device. The storage only sees encrypted blobs.
sync.e2eIrreversibleWarning: Warning: without this passphrase the data cannot be recovered. Store it somewhere safe.
sync.e2eRemoteRequiresPassphrase: This dataset is encrypted. Enter the passphrase to unlock this device's view of the data.
sync.passphraseChangeHint: Set a new passphrase for end-to-end encryption. The encrypted data itself stays unchanged — other devices that are already connected keep syncing. The new passphrase is only needed when connecting an additional device from now on.
sync.passphraseChangeErrorEmpty: Please fill in both passphrase fields.
sync.passphraseChangeErrorSame: The new passphrase must differ from the current one.
sync.passphraseChangeErrorAuth: The current passphrase is not correct.

syncConflicts.title: Sync conflicts
syncConflicts.intro_one: One field was edited differently on two devices. Pick which version to keep.
syncConflicts.intro_other: {{count}} fields were edited differently on two devices. Pick which version to keep for each.
syncConflicts.actionSaveBothUnsupported: "Save both" isn't available yet in this version.

statusCoupling.heading: Status coupling
statusCoupling.label: Couple parent and subtask status
statusCoupling.hint: When enabled, completing a parent task marks its open subtasks complete, and finishing every subtask marks the parent complete. Disable to treat each task independently — status changes never propagate up or down the tree.

autoDate.heading: Auto-date on start
autoDate.label: Pin a backlog task to today when work begins
autoDate.hint: When enabled, a task without a scheduled day gets today's date the moment its status flips to in progress — directly or via the cascade from a child. Disable to leave the scheduled day alone.

carryOverDefault.heading: Carry-over default
carryOverDefault.hint: On startup, decide what happens to tasks whose scheduled day has passed and that are still open. "Ask" opens the carry-over dialog; the other options run silently and announce the result.

dayStartTrigger.heading: Day-start trigger
dayStartTrigger.hint: When to run the carry-over, missed-deadline, and deadline-pin checks on a long-running app. "At midnight" fires as soon as the local date rolls over. Pick a morning hour to defer the dialog until you're at the desk. "App start only" disables the day-change re-check entirely (legacy behaviour).
dayStartTrigger.label: Trigger

perList.heading: Per task list
perList.hint: Override the three defaults above for individual task lists. Leave a field on "Global default" to inherit; pick a specific value to make this list behave differently from the rest.

privacyNotice.title: Privacy notice
privacyNotice.body: Aperio syncs your contacts directly with the connected provider and keeps the data in memory so the attendees picker and search stay responsive. Names, email addresses, phone numbers, birthdays, and organisation fields are kept; photos are loaded lazily on demand.
privacyNotice.providerLine: What {{provider}} collects and how long it's retained is governed by their privacy policy:
privacyNotice.providerGeneric: For CalDAV / CardDAV / iCloud / Exchange servers your provider's privacy policy applies — your administrator can point you at it if you need the exact link.
privacyNotice.cacheHint: You can clear the local cache at any time under Settings → Contacts → "Clear cache".

accounts.rowLabel: {{name}} ({{kind}}). Press Enter or Delete to remove.
accounts.rowLabelMissing: {{name}} ({{kind}}). Credentials missing on this device. Press Enter or Delete to remove.
accounts.missingCredentials_one: 1 account needs credentials on this device.
accounts.missingCredentials_other: {{count}} accounts need credentials on this device.
accounts.kindUnavailable: This adapter type is not available yet.
accounts.serverUrlHint: Hostname or full URL. The app discovers the CalDAV root automatically (RFC 6764).
accounts.passwordHint: Use an app-specific password where the provider offers one (iCloud, Fastmail, …). Stored only in your operating system's credential store.
accounts.testOk: Connection works. The calendars below will appear in the sidebar.
accounts.feedUrlHint: Public .ics URL. Read-only — events from this feed cannot be edited in Aperio.
accounts.icalAuthHint: Only fill in if the feed requires HTTP Basic auth. Public feeds stay anonymous.
accounts.googleClientIdHint: From your Google Cloud Console (APIs & Services → Credentials → OAuth 2.0 Client ID, type "Desktop App"). Aperio needs your own client ID until it ships its own verified Google app registration.
accounts.googleClientSecretHint: Sits right under the client ID in the same Cloud Console entry. Despite the name, Google's own docs concede the secret isn't actually secret for Desktop apps — Aperio stores it next to the client ID in the local DB.
accounts.googleFlowHint: Pressing "Add" opens your browser to Google's consent screen. After you grant access the tab closes itself and the calendar appears in the sidebar.
accounts.microsoftClientIdHint: From the Azure portal (Entra ID → App registrations → your app → Application (client) ID). Register the app as type "Public client/native (mobile & desktop)" with redirect URI "http://localhost".
accounts.microsoftAuthorityConsumers: Personal Microsoft accounts only (outlook.com, hotmail.com, live.com)
accounts.microsoftAuthorityHint: Must match your Azure app registration's "supported account types". "All" is usually right.
accounts.microsoftFlowHint: Pressing "Add" opens your browser to Microsoft's sign-in page. Unlike Google, no client secret is required — PKCE alone is enough.
accounts.ewsEndpointHint: The Exchange Web Services SOAP endpoint your server admin gave you. Always ends in "/EWS/Exchange.asmx". If you don't know the URL, fill in the e-mail + password fields below and press "Discover URL" — Aperio will ask Microsoft Autodiscover for you.
accounts.ewsEndpointRequired: Please enter the EWS endpoint URL.
accounts.ewsUsernameHint: Usually your full email address, but some servers want DOMAIN\\username. Ask your admin if unsure.
accounts.ewsReadOnlyHint: Full read/write — calendars and events sync both ways, including create, edit, delete and rename. Editing or deleting a recurring event affects the whole series; "delete only this occurrence" skips just that date.
accounts.ewsDiscoverNeedsEmail: Please enter your e-mail address before running Discover — autodiscover uses it to figure out which server to ask.
accounts.ewsDiscoverNeedsPassword: Please enter your password before running Discover — Microsoft's autodiscover endpoint requires Basic auth.
accounts.ewsDiscoverSrHint: Ask Microsoft Autodiscover for the EWS endpoint based on your e-mail address. Requires the e-mail and password fields above to be filled in.
accounts.vikunjaServerUrlHint: The base URL of your Vikunja instance — just the server root, no path. Aperio appends "/api/v1" itself.
accounts.vikunjaServerUrlRequired: Please enter the Vikunja server URL.
accounts.vikunjaApiTokenRequired: Please enter your Vikunja API token.
accounts.vikunjaApiTokenHint: Create a token in Vikunja under Settings → API Tokens. The token never leaves your system keychain after you press "Add".
accounts.todoistApiTokenRequired: Please enter your Todoist API token.
accounts.todoistApiTokenHint: Find your token in Todoist under Settings → Integrations → Developer → API token. The token never leaves your system keychain after you press "Add".
